data.name: TopicNavAriaLabelUi
data.value: Topics in the UI Design System

data.name: RootIntro
data.value: The beeday Experience System — the public, browsable record of how beeday looks, behaves, and communicates. The Brand System, the UI Design System, and the UX System formalized during EPIC 25, kept in sync with the product itself.

data.name: RootBrandCardDescription
data.value: Identity, wordmark, color, typography, illustration, characters, and writing.

data.name: RootUiCardDescription
data.value: Foundations, components, product patterns, interaction, and layout.

data.name: RootUxCardDescription
data.value: Accessibility, responsiveness, localization, motion, and performance.

data.name: RootClosingText
data.value: Every rule on these pages was formalized against the current beeday codebase — its components, tokens, tests, and resource catalogs — not decided in the abstract. Nothing here is a proposal.

data.name: BrandOverviewIntro
data.value: Identity, wordmark, logo, and brand color; expressive typography and imagery; illustration and characters; voice and tone. The Brand System governs how beeday presents itself as a brand — distinct from, and sharing foundations with, the UI Design System.

data.name: BrandIdentityCardDescription
data.value: The official brand name, casing, and color — and where brand identity ends and technical identity begins.

data.name: BrandWordmarkCardDescription
data.value: The two canonical representations of the beeday wordmark, and when each one applies.

data.name: BrandColorCardDescription
data.value: How brand, surface, content, semantic, product, illustration, and component colors are owned and used.

data.name: BrandTypographyCardDescription
data.value: Coiny for brand display, Nunito for product — and the roles that choose between them.

data.name: BrandIllustrationCardDescription
data.value: Shape language, composition rules, and the accessibility contract for beeday's artwork.

data.name: BrandCharactersCardDescription
data.value: The bee and six supporting characters — what the current artwork confirms, and what remains unknown.

data.name: BrandWritingCardDescription
data.value: Narrative, voice, tone by context, style, and the canonical bilingual glossary.

data.name: BrandIdentityIntro
data.value: beeday's brand identity is a small set of decisions, approved before EPIC 25 began, that apply everywhere the brand is presented — without needing to be rediscussed sprint by sprint.

data.name: BrandIdentityContractText
data.value: Three decisions define the visible brand, and they hold everywhere the name is presented as branding.

data.name: BrandIdentityContractCasingValue
data.value: lowercase — title case and all-caps styling are never the official visible form

data.name: BrandIdentityColorRuleText
data.value: Whenever the beeday name appears as a branding element, its color is #5247F9 — never an approximation and never substituted, except where a technical or accessibility context makes color representation inapplicable.

data.name: BrandIdentityBoundaryText
data.value: The brand decision above does not authorize a technical rename. The product's technical identity — the solution, namespaces, assemblies, component names, database, configuration keys, and infrastructure — remains unchanged until a specific, explicitly approved task changes it, backed by a full consumer and backward-compatibility analysis. Brand identity and technical identity are never the same decision.

data.name: BrandIdentityBoundaryItem1
data.value: The solution file and every project inside it

data.name: BrandIdentityBoundaryItem2
data.value: Every namespace under the product's technical root, and components such as BeeDayButton, BeeDayCard, and BeeDayIcon

data.name: BrandIdentityBoundaryItem3
data.value: The database context, migrations, and configuration keys

data.name: BrandIdentityBoundaryItem4
data.value: Cookies and the ASP.NET Core Data Protection application name

data.name: BrandIdentityDo1
data.value: Write the visible brand as beeday, always lowercase, in every language and surface.

data.name: BrandIdentityDo2
data.value: Use #5247F9 whenever the visible brand name carries color.

data.name: BrandIdentityAvoid1
data.value: Renaming technical namespaces, projects, or components to chase the visual brand.

data.name: BrandIdentityAvoid2
data.value: Styling the visible brand in title case or all caps.

data.name: BrandWordmarkIntro
data.value: beeday has two canonical wordmark representations. They are not competing versions — each was deliberately kept for a context the other does not cover.

data.name: BrandWordmarkTextText
data.value: BeeDayBrand renders the name as two literal text nodes, bee and day, entirely in Brand Primary (#5247F9), with role="img" and an accessible name of beeday. It is compact and chrome-scale, used in the authenticated shell — the desktop sidebar, the mobile sidebar, and the mobile header.

data.name: BrandWordmarkLockupText
data.value: The public header and footer use a raster lockup: the bee illustration together with the wordmark, at hero scale (866×288), already lowercase and already in the official brand color. It was preserved as-is rather than converged into BeeDayBrand — replacing it would remove the bee illustration from the two most visible public surfaces, and would require a hero-scale sizing contract BeeDayBrand does not have today.

data.name: BrandWordmarkCalloutText
data.value: Both representations satisfy the brand contract — lowercase, official color — so neither one is waiting to be fixed. Which one a future component should use is a decision this page reports, not one it makes.

data.name: BrandColorIntro
data.value: Every color token in beeday belongs to one of seven categories, owned by meaning rather than by hex value.

data.name: BrandColorTaxonomyText
data.value: The same physical value can legitimately serve two different categories at once — #FFFFFF is Background, Surface, and Text Inverse at the same time — because ownership follows meaning, not hex equivalence.

data.name: BrandColorCategoryBrandText
data.value: Official identity and its directly derived states

data.name: BrandColorCategorySemanticText
data.value: Feedback independent of feature — success, warning, danger, information

data.name: BrandColorCategoryIllustrationText
data.value: Artistic composition values, not automatically promoted to UI tokens

data.name: BrandColorCategoryComponentText
data.value: Aliases that stabilize one primitive's implementation

data.name: BrandColorStatesText
data.value: #5247F9 is the only approved brand color. Hover, active, light, and soft are derived states of the same family — not additional brand colors.

data.name: BrandColorYellowTitle
data.value: Brand Yellow is Product/Reward, not a second brand color

data.name: BrandColorYellowText
data.value: #FFD326 was evaluated and classified Semantic/Component under Product/Reward ownership — its real consumers are the experience bar and the reward tone of the progress bar, not brand identity. The public brand-yellow tokens still resolve to the same values for backward compatibility, but new work should consume the reward tokens directly.

data.name: BrandColorHardcodeText
data.value: A hardcoded value is only promoted to a token when meaning, reuse, ownership, and real consumers justify it — a token created for a single consumer is its own kind of debt. Illustration values, product-specific values, and values still awaiting a convergence sprint are deliberately preserved as local literals rather than forced into premature tokens.

data.name: BrandIllustrationIntro
data.value: beeday's artwork follows a consistent shape language and a small set of composition rules, extracted directly from the seven approved assets and their consumers — not prescribed in the abstract.

data.name: BrandIllustrationShape1
data.value: Geometry: simple, rounded, inflated masses; edges, snouts, ears, and accessories avoid dominant sharp corners.

data.name: BrandIllustrationShape2
data.value: Contour: no uniform external outline — separation comes from color changes, occlusion, highlights, and soft shadows.

data.name: BrandIllustrationShape3
data.value: Volume and perspective: stylized 3D rendering, front or three-quarter view, with body overlap suggesting depth.

data.name: BrandIllustrationShape4
data.value: Light: soft highlights, contact shadows, and diffuse colored glow — never hard UI shadows, hatching, or realistic texture.

data.name: BrandIllustrationShape5
data.value: Color: the bee's yellow and the brand's violet/blue coexist with orange, brown, pink, green, and cyan specific to the artwork — these artistic colors remain Illustration and are not automatically Brand, Semantic, or Product tokens.

data.name: BrandIllustrationComposition1
data.value: Use the complete approved groups in their two approved contexts — the individual bee art belongs to the how-it-works section and does not substitute for the group compositions, or the other way around.

data.name: BrandIllustrationComposition2
data.value: Preserve the intrinsic aspect ratio with height: auto or object-fit: contain — artwork is never stretched to fill a box.

data.name: BrandIllustrationComposition3
data.value: Never crop a character, antenna, wing, ear, or the flower. The only approved crop is the wave's vertical crop, controlled by its own container.

data.name: BrandIllustrationComposition4
data.value: Keep text and controls outside the art. Illustration never intercepts pointer input or covers focus, labels, or controls.

data.name: BrandIllustrationA11yText
data.value: All current artwork is decorative: the surrounding heading, steps, and links already communicate the full content, so every image is marked decorative and hidden from assistive technology. The Home hero stays above the fold and loads with high priority; the three images below it use lazy loading and asynchronous decoding. Declared width and height are always kept to reserve proportion and reduce layout shift. The four artistic PNGs together weigh about 4.6 MB with no responsive variants today — that is documented debt, not a silent gap, and any future optimization must be validated visually at the existing breakpoints.

data.name: BrandCharactersIntro
data.value: beeday's cast is documented exactly as far as the approved artwork proves — no names, lore, or anatomy are invented to fill the gaps.

data.name: BrandCharactersBeeText
data.value: The bee is the central character: it is the only one with an individually named file, it occupies the largest foreground in the hero, and it reappears in the closing group. The repository does not establish a proper name, gender, age, personality, or biography.

data.name: BrandCharactersBee1
data.value: Rounded, compact silhouette; roughly circular body; two antennae with spherical tips; two dark stripes; translucent side wings; short limbs.

data.name: BrandCharactersBee2
data.value: Approved artwork covers open-mouth joy, closed-eyes joy, and a dynamic pose — no other emotion is approved today.

data.name: BrandCharactersBee3
data.value: No approved composition crops the bee's silhouette — antennae and wings stay fully inside the frame.

data.name: BrandCharactersCastText
data.value: The same six supporting characters appear in both group compositions. The labels below are visual descriptions, not official names.

data.name: BrandCharactersCastFoxTraits
data.value: Pointed ears, light snout and tail, purple bow, light shirt, blue overalls

data.name: BrandCharactersCastBearTraits
data.value: Round ears, light snout, blue shirt, purple pants or shorts with a belt

data.name: BrandCharactersCastCatTraits
data.value: Dark stripes, red band, red shorts

data.name: BrandCharactersCastPrimateTraits
data.value: Light face and ears, curved tail, yellow shirt with a blue trim

data.name: BrandCharactersCastWhiteCatTraits
data.value: Triangular ears, pink bow, pink outfit with a light top

data.name: BrandCharactersCastFlowerTraits
data.value: Yellow petals, brown face, green leaves and stem, green pot

data.name: BrandCharactersAvoid1
data.value: Inventing names, exact species, personalities, or lore beyond what the approved artwork shows.

data.name: BrandCharactersAvoid2
data.value: Extracting or cropping an individual character out of a group composition.

data.name: BrandWritingIntro
data.value: beeday helps build a better day, one step at a time. The approved narrative connects what matters to concrete action — organizing Daily, habits, tasks, and projects, tracking progress, and recognizing consistent advancement — without promising instant transformation, perfect productivity, or results the product does not compute.

data.name: BrandWritingVoice1
data.value: Clear — concrete words, names the object of the action, avoids slogans in place of instruction.

data.name: BrandWritingVoice2
data.value: Encouraging — recognizes progress without infantilizing, pressuring, or assigning blame.

data.name: BrandWritingVoice3
data.value: Action-oriented — verbs say what to do, feedback confirms what happened.

data.name: BrandWritingVoice4
data.value: Honest — distinguishes success, failure, and partial state, without hiding consequences or inventing benefits.

data.name: BrandWritingVoice5
data.value: Close, not invasive — speaks directly with "you" and "your" without assuming emotion, routine, or personal goals.

data.name: BrandWritingToneNeutralValue
data.value: Direct and calm — state or action in a few words

data.name: BrandWritingToneOnboardingValue
data.value: Welcoming — real benefit plus next step, never artificial urgency

data.name: BrandWritingToneErrorValue
data.value: Factual and recoverable — what failed, what was preserved, a retry when one exists

data.name: BrandWritingToneDestructiveValue
data.value: Unambiguous and sober — verb plus object, permanent consequence stated separately

data.name: BrandWritingToneWalletValue
data.value: Precise and restrained — value, type, date, effect, and reversibility, never a judgment

data.name: BrandWritingStyle1
data.value: The visual brand is always beeday, even mid-sentence, in a heading, or inside a button — never Title Case.

data.name: BrandWritingStyle2
data.value: New product copy uses sentence case for headings, labels, and buttons.

data.name: BrandWritingStyle3
data.value: A CTA starts with a specific verb — Create transaction, Try again — and still reads correctly outside its surrounding paragraph.

data.name: BrandWritingStyle4
data.value: Headings, labels, tabs, and toast titles do not take a final period.

data.name: BrandWritingStyle5
data.value: XP is an invariant, uppercase abbreviation in both languages; Level localizes to Nível in Portuguese.

data.name: BrandWritingStyle6
data.value: Wallet always represents USD — the $ sign is fixed, while grouping, decimals, and symbol position follow the active culture.

data.name: BrandWritingGlossaryActivityMeaning
data.value: Umbrella term for Habit, Task, and To-Do — never replaces the specific subtype in the UI

data.name: BrandWritingGlossaryHabitMeaning
data.value: Recurring behavior with progress or a counter

data.name: BrandWritingGlossaryTaskMeaning
data.value: Recurring or repeatable activity, completed manually

data.name: BrandWritingGlossaryTodoMeaning
data.value: Action that belongs to exactly one Project

data.name: BrandWritingGlossaryDailyMeaning
data.value: Surface that organizes the day's activities

data.name: BrandWritingGlossaryXpMeaning
data.value: Unit of Experience — an invariant abbreviation

data.name: UiOverviewPageTitle
data.value: UI Design System | beeday Experience System

data.name: UiOverviewIntro
data.value: Foundations and semantic tokens; components, states, and layouts; forms, navigation, surfaces, and feedback; responsive behavior and accessibility contracts; interaction. The UI Design System is the shared component tree that every product page composes from — not a separately published library.

data.name: UiFoundationsCardDescription
data.value: Typography roles, spacing, shape, motion, and the shared layer order.

data.name: UiComponentsCardDescription
data.value: The 26 shared contracts — no V2, no parallel component library.

data.name: UiProductPatternsCardDescription
data.value: Where a specialized pattern is legitimate, and where it is not.

data.name: UiInteractionCardDescription
data.value: The state matrix, microinteractions, and the shared dialog lifecycle.

data.name: UiLayoutCardDescription
data.value: The three layouts, the shell breakpoint, and shared containers.

data.name: UiFoundationsIntro
data.value: Typography, spacing, shape, motion, and layering are the tokens every shared component and product page is built from. Color foundations are covered on their own page — see Color in the Brand System.

data.name: UiFoundationsTypographyProductUse
data.value: Body, navigation, buttons, labels, forms, captions, product headings

data.name: UiFoundationsTypographyBrandUse
data.value: Large, expressive brand moments only — never controls or long-form reading

data.name: UiFoundationsSpacingText
data.value: A single linear scale of nine steps, all in rem, shared by every layout and component.

data.name: UiFoundationsShapeText
data.value: Seven radius steps, chosen by role rather than by component: controls and inputs use lg; cards default to lg and reserve 2xl for prominent or showcase moments; dialogs use lg; pills and chips use pill; true circles — avatars, markers — use 50%, never pill.

data.name: UiFoundationsMotionText
data.value: Three shared durations and two easings cover hover, state change, and panel motion. Every shared motion change needs a local prefers-reduced-motion fallback — the count stands at 23 of 31 production stylesheets today, tracked as an open item rather than claimed complete.

data.name: UiFoundationsDurationFastText
data.value: Hover, pressed, and immediate visual response

data.name: UiFoundationsDurationSlowText
data.value: Panels and drawers with noticeable displacement

data.name: UiFoundationsLayerText
data.value: Shared z-index values only apply when an element needs to compete outside its local stacking context, in this fixed order:

data.name: UiFoundationsLayerOrder
data.value: Navigation → Drawer backdrop → Drawer → Dropdown → Modal → Raised modal → Destructive confirmation → Loading → Toast

data.name: UiComponentsIntro
data.value: 26 shared contracts — 25 primitives under Components/DesignSystem plus BeeDaySortable — cover the product's actions, feedback, forms, layout, and progress. There is no V2 of any component and no parallel component library; the governance rule is reuse, then extend, then consolidate, then refactor, and create only when nothing existing fits.

data.name: UiComponentsButtonText
data.value: The canonical action — eight variants, loading and disabled states, always keeps an accessible name.

data.name: UiComponentsCardText
data.value: A stateless content surface; interactive semantics belong to the consumer.

data.name: UiComponentsConfirmDialogText
data.value: Destructive confirmation only, never a general-purpose modal.

data.name: UiComponentsToastText
data.value: The result of a mutation — success or error — always the last thing that happens after saving or deleting.

data.name: UiComponentsEmptyStateText
data.value: Title, description, and an optional icon; the action is composed by the caller.

data.name: UiComponentsFormsText
data.value: Six form components share one contract: label, disabled, validation flag, and a two-way bound value — none of them inherit the framework's InputBase.

data.name: UiComponentsIconText
data.value: The only icon primitive. Decorative by default; an informative icon requires an explicit, non-empty label and is validated at render time.

data.name: UiComponentsHeadersText
data.value: PageHeader, SectionHeader, and Hero share one eyebrow-title-description-actions shape at three different scales.

data.name: UiComponentsEditorModalText
data.value: The shared editor shell — three slots, three callbacks, and the same focus lifecycle as every other dialog.

data.name: UiComponentsBrandText
data.value: The inline wordmark primitive — see Wordmark in the Brand System.

data.name: UiComponentsProgressText
data.value: Receives a ready value; it never computes XP or task completion itself.

data.name: UiComponentsSortableText
data.value: Drag, touch, and keyboard reordering with a single shared ownership of the result.

data.name: UiComponentsCalloutText
data.value: Reuse, then extend, then consolidate, then refactor — create a new primitive only when none of the previous steps can honestly solve the problem.

data.name: UiProductPatternsIntro
data.value: A Product Pattern is a feature-specific specialization built from shared primitives — not a shortcut around them. It stays specialized when the difference it encodes is semantically real, and it converges when the difference turns out to be accidental.

data.name: UiProductPatternsWalletText
data.value: Wallet composes a compact BeeDayHero, cards, buttons, empty states, and the shared editor and confirm dialogs. Monetary formatting and income/expense semantics remain product-specific specializations, while Tag color now draws from the same shared COR0-COR9 palette token hero surfaces use, instead of a free-form picker.

data.name: UiProductPatternsDailyText
data.value: Daily preserves four distinct concepts — Habit, Task, To-Do, and Project — with their own colors, metrics, and actions; physical equality between two values never authorizes collapsing their meaning. Manual ordering is owned by BeeDaySortable, not by an implicit sort.

data.name: UiProductPatternsEmptyText
data.value: WalletEmptyState chooses copy and an action for zero transactions or a filtered zero-result state, then delegates the actual surface to the shared EmptyState — the visual pattern is one, the composition is feature-owned.

data.name: UiProductPatternsCalloutText
data.value: Login and CreateProfile keep native HTML controls rather than the shared form components, because they must preserve exact field names, antiforgery tokens, and a login endpoint contract that predates EditContext — they still consume the same visual field chrome as every other form.

data.name: UiInteractionIntro
data.value: A formal state matrix and a small set of interaction rules apply across every shared component, so that hover, focus, and busy states mean the same thing everywhere in the product.

data.name: UiInteractionRule1
data.value: Hover never substitutes for focus-visible — both are always available independently.

data.name: UiInteractionRule2
data.value: Pressed and active confirm an action without reflowing anything outside the control.

data.name: UiInteractionRule3
data.value: Disabled stops both interaction and motion.

data.name: UiInteractionRule4
data.value: Loading and busy states preserve the component's accessible name and semantics.

data.name: UiInteractionRule5
data.value: Selected and expanded states are exposed through a real attribute, never through color alone.

data.name: UiInteractionMicroHoverText
data.value: A small upward shift plus a raised shadow

data.name: UiInteractionMicroPressText
data.value: A physical downward displacement, like a real button sinking

data.name: UiInteractionMicroEnterText
data.value: A fade with a subtle scale, for a newly added list item

data.name: UiInteractionMicroReorderText
data.value: A short scale bounce after a dragged card is dropped in its new place

data.name: UiInteractionDialogText
data.value: Confirm, Editor, and Feedback dialogs share the smallest common behavior — open, move initial focus, contain Tab and Shift+Tab, close on Escape, and restore focus to the trigger — without sharing markup or meaning beyond that lifecycle.

data.name: UiLayoutIntro
data.value: Three layouts host every route in the product, and one structural breakpoint decides which navigation paradigm the authenticated shell uses.

data.name: UiLayoutMainStructure
data.value: Mobile header plus desktop sidebar and workspace, plus mobile sidebar

data.name: UiLayoutPublicUse
data.value: The public Home and the beeday Experience System

data.name: UiLayoutPublicStructure
data.value: Public header, page content, and the institutional footer

data.name: UiLayoutOnboardingUse
data.value: Login, Identity, and the initial profile and tutorial flow

data.name: UiLayoutShellText
data.value: 1200px is the only breakpoint that swaps the authenticated shell's entire navigation paradigm: at or above it, the desktop sidebar is fixed and the workspace is offset by its width; below it, a mobile header and an overlay sidebar take over and the workspace uses its full width. 1024px belongs to the tablet range of that same shell, not to a separate desktop paradigm.

data.name: UiLayoutContainersText
data.value: Public pages share a fluid gutter and a 72rem reading width; the header and footer use a container capped at 1440px. Authenticated pages remove that global width so Daily, Wallet, and Profile can each own their layout without being forced into the same container.

data.name: UiLayoutBreakpointFamiliesText
data.value: 42rem (672px) coordinates the public header, language switcher, and header primitives; 40rem (640px) is the compact family shared by Auth, Onboarding, the footer, and Brand Guidelines pages including this Experience System.

data.name: UxOverviewIntro
data.value: What the product guarantees today for accessibility, responsiveness, localization, motion, and performance — described as verified behavior, not as a wish list.

data.name: UxAccessibilityCardDescription
data.value: ARIA patterns, keyboard and focus lifecycle, reduced motion, and automated contrast.

data.name: UxResponsiveCardDescription
data.value: The regression viewports and the breakpoints that actually change structure.

data.name: UxLocalizationCardDescription
data.value: How culture is resolved, persisted, and applied — and what never gets translated.

data.name: UxMotionCardDescription
data.value: Shared durations, easings, and the reduced-motion contract.

data.name: UxPerformanceCardDescription
data.value: Image and font loading discipline, and the gaps that are tracked, not hidden.

data.name: UxAccessibilityIntro
data.value: What the code guarantees today, and where it does not — none of the statements on this page are aspirational.

data.name: UxAccessibilityAriaText
data.value: Destructive confirmation uses role="alertdialog"; the editor and feedback dialogs use role="dialog"; the toast host switches between role="status" and role="alert" by severity; busy regions expose aria-busy; decorative icons default to aria-hidden. Every dynamic ARIA boolean is serialized in lowercase.

data.name: UxAccessibilityFocusText
data.value: Every canonical dialog follows the same lifecycle: open, move initial focus, contain Tab and Shift+Tab, close on Escape, and restore focus — recalculated on every Tab press to respect busy and disabled controls. Focus-visible is styled globally with a ring derived from Brand Primary, complemented by generous scroll margin so a focused target never lands under a fixed header.

data.name: UxAccessibilityMotionText
data.value: 23 of 31 production stylesheets with animation, transition, or keyframes carry a local prefers-reduced-motion fallback today; the rest rely on a universal safety net that shortens duration but does not replace a proper local fallback. Reduced motion never hides feedback — loading keeps its label visible without a spinner, and menus and modals still appear, just without an animated entrance.

data.name: UxAccessibilityContrastText
data.value: An automated gate resolves real tokens from the foundation and applies the WCAG relative-luminance formula to nine deterministic pairs — brand, primary and secondary text, the four semantic buttons, information, and inverse focus. Secondary text on Surface measures about 8.69:1, comfortably above the AA and AAA thresholds for normal text; muted text on Surface measures about 4.26:1, which clears the large-text threshold but sits below 4.5:1 for normal-size text, so it is not used where that guarantee matters.

data.name: UxAccessibilityDisclaimerText
data.value: Automated scanning covers a representative sample of public and authenticated pages and a canonical dialog, without exclusions — a clean result means no automatically detectable violation in that sample, not WCAG conformance, legal certification, or a substitute for manual keyboard and screen-reader review.

data.name: UxResponsiveIntro
data.value: Breakpoints stay as literal values next to the component that owns them — CSS custom properties are not valid inside a media feature — but the structural ones are shared contracts, coordinated across files and protected by tests.

data.name: UxResponsiveViewportsText
data.value: Automated coverage exercises mobile (390 and 430px), tablet (768, 900, 1024, and 1199px), the desktop boundary (1200px), and wide desktop (1280, 1440, and 1920px) — chosen for real structural change, not for generic labels like "tablet."

data.name: UxResponsiveShellText
data.value: 1200px is the one breakpoint that changes the authenticated shell's navigation paradigm end to end; Daily's own board aligns to the same 1199/1200 pair to control its internal overflow.

data.name: UxResponsiveFamiliesText
data.value: 42rem coordinates the public header and header primitives; 40rem is the compact family shared by Auth, Onboarding, the footer, and Brand Guidelines pages, including this Experience System.

data.name: UxResponsiveOverflowText
data.value: No public document is allowed to produce horizontal overflow at the regression viewports; only the Daily board may scroll horizontally, and only inside its own container, never widening the page itself.

data.name: UxLocalizationIntro
data.value: beeday supports en-US and pt-BR today, resolved fresh on every request rather than sniffed from the browser.

data.name: UxLocalizationPrecedenceText
data.value: An explicit culture cookie always wins when present. Without one, an authenticated request falls back to the account's saved language preference and writes the cookie for next time. A request with neither signal resolves to en-US, the default culture — there is no browser Accept-Language sniffing.

data.name: UxLocalizationCatalogText
data.value: Every resource family follows the same four-file shape: a neutral fallback, an en-US file identical to the neutral one, and a pt-BR translation. An automated contract fails the build if any catalog loses key parity, if the neutral fallback drifts from en-US, or if a translation drops a placeholder.

data.name: UxLocalizationNever1
data.value: User-generated content — habit, task, and project titles, notes, tag names.

data.name: UxLocalizationNever2
data.value: Technical and ISO values — date input values, datetime attributes, correlation IDs, routes.

data.name: UxLocalizationNever3
data.value: The brand name beeday, the XP abbreviation, and the Tag concept — by current product decision.

data.name: UxMotionIntro
data.value: A small shared vocabulary of durations and easings covers hover, state change, and panel motion across the product, with reduced motion treated as a first-class contract rather than an afterthought.

data.name: UxMotionTaxonomy1
data.value: Micro-interaction — a short hover, press, or selection cue that is never the only signal of state.

data.name: UxMotionTaxonomy2
data.value: State transition — a color, border, opacity, or size change that explains a real update.

data.name: UxMotionTaxonomy3
data.value: Entrance and exit — drawers, menus, modals, and toasts, always respecting focus order.

data.name: UxMotionTaxonomy4
data.value: Loading and progress — spinners, shimmer, and progress bars; the reduced alternative keeps surface and text visible.

data.name: UxMotionTaxonomy5
data.value: Feedback and celebration — confirmation and experience gains, with the semantic content preserved when the animation is removed.

data.name: UxMotionTaxonomy6
data.value: Brand and decorative — optional expressive composition that never blocks reading or navigation.

data.name: UxMotionReducedTitle
data.value: Reduced motion is a contract, not a bonus

data.name: UxMotionReducedText
data.value: Every shared motion change needs a local prefers-reduced-motion fallback that removes translation, pulse, and repetition without hiding feedback — loading keeps its capsule visible, reconnect keeps its dialog and a static indicator, and menus still appear, just without an animated entrance. Coverage today stands at 23 of 31 production stylesheets, tracked openly rather than rounded up.

data.name: UxPerformanceIntro
data.value: Loading discipline is applied where it is verifiable today — image priority, lazy loading, and font delivery — without claiming metrics that are not actually measured.

data.name: UxPerformanceImagesText
data.value: The one hero image that renders above the fold loads with high fetch priority; every image below the fold uses lazy loading and asynchronous decoding. Width and height are always declared to reserve proportion and reduce layout shift.

data.name: UxPerformanceFontsText
data.value: Coiny and Nunito are delivered through Google Fonts with a preconnect hint and font-display: swap, so text stays visible while the brand or product typeface finishes loading.

data.name: UxPerformanceGapsText
data.value: There is no responsive image pipeline or srcset today, and real-world LCP and CLS are not measured — both are documented gaps, not silent ones. The four artistic PNGs on the Home page weigh about 4.6 MB combined with no responsive variants; any future optimization must be validated visually before it ships.

data.name: UxPerformanceDisclaimerText
data.value: These practices describe verified loading behavior, not a performance certification or an enforced budget.
